{{Use British English|date=February 2018}}

'''Derek Almey Ratcliffe''' (9 July 1929 – 23 May 2005) was one of the most significant [[England|English]] nature conservationists of the 20th century. He was Chief Scientist for the [[Nature Conservancy Council]] at the [[Monks Wood Experimental Station]], Abbots Ripton, Huntingdon, retiring in 1989. Ratcliffe was the author of the 1977 [[Nature Conservation Review]], a document which set out the most important sites for [[nature conservation]] in the [[United Kingdom]]. He also published various works on nature and conservation.

== Biography ==

Derek Ratcliffe grew up in Carlisle, and married his wife, Jeannette, in March 1978.<ref name="BritWildlife">Obituary, Des Thompson & H.J.B. Birks ''British Wildlife'' Vol. 16 No.6 pp. 410–412, August 2005 {{ISSN|0958-0956}}</ref><ref name="guardianobit">{{cite news |last1=Thompson |first1=Des |title=Obituary: Derek Ratcliffe |url=https://www.theguardian.com/news/2005/may/31/guardianobituaries.society |access-date=29 December 2020 |work=the Guardian |date=30 May 2005 |language=en}}</ref>

Ratcliffe was the first person to discover the link between the use by farmers of [[pesticides]]—such as [[DDT]] and [[Dieldrin]]—and the decline of British populations of birds of prey, particularly the [[peregrine falcon]].<ref name="guardianobit" />

He was instrumental in persuading the UK government to end the tax advantages available for planting non-native [[conifer]] forests on Scottish [[peat|peat bogs]], which was threatening the internationally important large wetland area of [[Caithness]] and [[Sutherland]] known as the [[Flow Country]].

Ratcliffe studied for a PhD at the [[Bangor University|University of Wales, Bangor]], completing it in 1953. He then undertook [[National Service]].<ref name="BritWildlife" /> He was awarded the [[British Trust for Ornithology]]'s [[Bernard Tucker Medal]] in 1964.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bto.org/aboutBTO/accounts/medallists.htm|title=Medallists|date=2006-06-02|publisher=BTO|access-date=2008-12-01}}</ref>

One of his most often cited works is a study on [[egg shell]] breakage conducted in the 1960s.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Ratcliffe, D. A.|title=Changes Attributable to Pesticides in Egg Breakage Frequency and Eggshell Thickness in some British Birds|journal=Journal of Applied Ecology|jstor=2401613|doi=10.2307/2401613|volume=7|issue=1|pages=67–115 |year=1970|bibcode=1970JApEc...7...67R |url=https://www.calvin.edu/~rpruim/courses/m143/articles/Ratcliffe-Eggshells-1970.pdf}}</ref> Some, including [[Rachel Carson]] in her book ''[[Silent Spring]]'', have interpreted the study as establishing a causal link between [[DDT]] contamination and thinning of egg shells in [[Bird of prey|raptors]].

Among his many other <ref>{{cite journal|pmid=6049131|year=1967|last1=Ratcliffe|first1=DA|title=Decrease in eggshell weight in certain birds of prey|doi=10.1038/215208a0|volume=215|issue=5097|pages=208–10|journal=Nature|bibcode=1967Natur.215..208R |s2cid=4175038}}</ref> studies of the topic are papers on the effect on specific bird species, such as the [[peregrine falcon]],<ref>{{cite journal|title=Studies of the recent breeding success of the peregrine, ''Falco peregrinus''|pmid=4522385|year=1973|last1=Ratcliffe|first1=DA|volume=19|pages=377–89|journal=Journal of Reproduction and Fertility. Supplement}}</ref> the [[raven]],<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Marquiss, M. |author2=Newton, I. |author3=Ratcliffe, D. A. |title=The Decline of the Raven, ''Coruvs Corax'', in Relation to Afforestation in Southern Scotland and Northern England |journal=Journal of Applied Ecology|volume=15|issue=1|pages=129–144|jstor=2402925|url=https://www.calvin.edu/~rpruim/courses/m143/articles/Ratcliffe-BirdsOfPrey.pdf|doi=10.2307/2402925|year=1978|bibcode=1978JApEc..15..129M }}</ref> In these studies he developed "Ratcliffe's Index," considered "a reliable measure of relative shell thickness" <ref>{{cite journal|author1=Burnham, William A. |author2=Enderson, James H. |author3=Boardman, Thomas J. |title=Variation in Peregrine Falcon Eggs|journal=The Auk|volume= 101|pages=578–583|issue=3 |year=1984|doi=10.1093/auk/101.3.578 |url=http://sora.unm.edu/sites/default/files/journals/auk/v101n03/p0578-p0583.pdf}}</ref>

==Publications==
Derek Ratcliffe's most important publications include:
* ''Plant Communities of the Scottish Highlands'' (1962, with Donald McVean)
* ''[[A Nature Conservation Review]]'' (1977 {{ISBN|0-521-21159-X}})
* ''The Peregrine Falcon'' (Poyser, 1980; expanded second edition 1993)
* ''Bird Life of Mountain and Upland'' (Cambridge University Press, 1991 {{ISBN|0-521-33123-4}})
* ''The Raven'' (Poyser, 1997)
* ''In Search of Nature'' (Broadfield, 2000)
* ''Lakeland'' (Collins [[New Naturalist]], 2002 {{ISBN|0-00-711304-8}})
* ''Lapland: a natural history'' (Poyser, 2005 {{ISBN|0-7136-6529-7}})
* ''Galloway and the Borders'' (Collins [[New Naturalist]], 2007 {{ISBN|0-00-717401-2}}. Completed a few days before his death in 2005)
